figures.finding: From 1 April 2026 a resident's chargeable income is taxed at 20% up to M77,760 a year (M6,480 a month) and 30% above, less a non-refundable personal tax credit of M12,240 a year (M1,020 a month).
figures.applies: Tax year from 1 April 2026; the RSL's 2026-27 employment-income guide states the monthly band and credit.

sources.said: Any chargeable income from M 1.00 up to M 6, 480.00 per month is taxable at 20%; and … Any excess of M 6, 480.00 per month is taxable at 30%. … Individuals are granted a non-refundable tax credit of M1,020.00 per month.

figures.finding: The 2026/27 tax year begins on 1 April 2026.

sources.said: The above change is effective 1 April 2026 .

figures.finding: Employers withhold PAYE monthly at 20% to M6,480 and 30% above, less the M1,020 monthly credit, and remit it to the RSL by the 15th of the next month.

sources.said: Any chargeable income from M 1.00 up to M 6, 480.00 per month is taxable at 20%; and … Any excess of M 6, 480.00 per month is taxable at 30%. … has the obligation to remit the tax to the Revenue Services Lesotho by the 15th of every month following the month of deduction.

figures.finding: A payer withholds 10% of the gross from a non-resident artiste's or entertainer's fee under a Lesotho-source services contract (s. 108), and 25% from royalties paid to a non-resident (s. 107); the non-resident may file a return if the withholding exceeds the tax otherwise due, so it is final unless a return is filed.
figures.applies: Income Tax Act 1993 ss. 107-108 as set out in the 2010 public ruling still posted by the RSL; later rate changes not read.

sources.said: In terms of section 108, tax is withheld where payment is made to a non-resident under a Lesotho source services contract. … Artistes; Entertainers; Sportspersons; Auditing; Accounting; Economic; Financial; Legal; Engineering; Architectural; etc. WD3(1993) 10% … Optional for all items in this category … Royalty WD1 (1993) WD1 (1993) WD5 (1993) WD4 (1993) WD5 (1993) 25% … the words “Optional” apply where the law allows filing of a return if the taxpayer feels that the income tax paid during the tax year, by way of withholding, is higher than that which is otherwise payable

blockers.sought: The VAT rate and registration threshold for a freelancer: the RSL's VAT 101 guide prints the threshold as 'M 2000,000.00 per annum', which reads as either M2,000,000 or a misprint (its own example treats M200,150 of sales in six months as reaching it); the rate is not in the guide. Also still sought: social contributions on pay and the individual return due date.
